utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Good morning. Could we have the case called, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-32/1-PT, The Prosecutor versus Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to make sure that what is being said in the courtroom is also understood by the two accused, I would appreciate if you could nod in assent if you do. Mr. Milan Lukic. Mr. Sredoje Lukic. That seems to be the case. Thank you. Could we then have the representation please, Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Well, the point is that you should read whatever you want to read into the record so we have the representation on the record I can. I would be grateful if you could indicate who is representing the prosecution at today's Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, I was waiting for your approval to do so. I am Frederic Ossogo. I represent the OTP in the absence of Mr. Mark Harmon. I'm together with Mr. Stevan Cole who is also a member of the OTP and our team. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ossogo. And we have a new counsel representing Mr. Milan Lukic, and I take you first since you are a new comer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SULEJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I am in this courtroom for the first time. I have been appointed, as you know, on the 5th of December. My name is Bojan Sulejic. I'm an attorney from Belgrade; and, hopefully, by the end of the -- I will successfully represent Mr. Milan Lukic until this case is concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sulejic. And let me formally welcome you to the case and hope that your contributions will be of a productive nature. Thank you. And for Mr. Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Good morning. My name is Jens Dieckmann. I'm co-counsel for Mr. Sredoje Lukic, and I represent today our team. Mr. Cepic apologise. He is preparing his Defence witnesses in the Milutinovic case, and that is the reason he is not here. I'm assisted by Yvonne Mitri, as lead assistant, and, legal assistant of Ms. Cepic, Ms. Sladana Marijonovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Dieckmann. Let me then, first, proceed with the Chamber's understanding as to outstanding motions; and as far as I can see, there are not that many; in fact, only one. It goes go back to disclosure matters. There was a decision taken by the -- by the Chamber on the 5th of November, 2007, allowing for late disclosure of some five witnesses, witnesses to be disclosed not earlier than 30 days prior to trial; and then there was an option for the Prosecution to deal with another eight witnesses, an option which the Prosecution decided to exercise by actually disclosing them to the Defence, and that happened on the 9th of November. Regarding the five witnesses who are not disclosed and where protective measures were sought, the Prosecution moved on the 4th of December, in relation to additional protective measures for those witnesses. That motion is still open, meaning it is time running for the Defence to respond to it; and once the response is in, the Chamber will obviously decide on the matter. As far as the Chamber can see, there aren't any other open or live issues at the moment. Is this the understanding of the parties as well? I turn first to the Prosecution, Mr. Ossogo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is right, Your Honour. Let me just add that in the latest motion we filed on the 4th of December, we also moved for an extension of time until the 30th of January, 2008 for one of the witnesses for whom we have some problem contacting him. We explained this in an ex parte annex to the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ossogo. That part of the motion was noticed by the Chamber as well. I just want to make sure that my understanding as to the situation at hand squares with yours as well, Mr. Dieckmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Due to the point of the Defence, the description is correct, and we don't have any comment about it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Dieckmann. Mr. Sulejic, do you have any other position, different from Mr. Dieckmann?

utterances.speaker: MR. SULEJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, and I would like to ask you at this point, since I have not had that much time to acquaint myself with the case file, to give me some sort of instruction and a little bit of time in order to be able to respond to all of the questions that might potentially appear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Sulejic. We certainly appreciate that are you a relative new comer to the case, and I also understand that Mr. Yatvin, who earlier had the position that you now hold, has or should hand over all the material he has and obviously relate to you any other information that he deems proper in order for you to be able to conduct your Defence of Mr. Milan Lukic as efficiently and as proper as possible. Let me just at this moment say that obviously all the decisions that have been taken - and I'm thinking primarily of all the dates which is entailed in the work plan, which was adopted by the Chamber at an earlier Status Conference - those times certainly do apply; but just to make sure there is no misunderstanding before we leave today, I will have a run through the times. So you, Mr. Sulejic, will have an opportunity to take further note of it; and if there is any particular need for your case to have an extension, we may come back to one point, I think, which should be of concern to you. But apart from that, I think what is laid down, as far as time-limits, applies also to you and your client, Mr. Sulejic. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. SULEJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I understand everything. The only thing that I'm concerned about is the deadline that was actually expiring the day before yesterday. That is my only request possibly to get an extension at this point in time, so that I have time to go through everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sulejic. I believe you refer to the deadline set for giving notice under Rule 67, and I will come back to that matter. So it is not forgotten, but thank you for reminding me. And with that, I intend just to proceed in order to make sure that what is discussed with the senior legal officer yesterday, in preparation of today's meeting, also is the same as I had been told. It seems that when we look at the disclosure matters, which we also touched upon when we touched upon the question of open motions, all material, as far as Rule 66(A)(i), I'm told have all been disclosed and received. Is that correct? I turn to the Defence because it is your interest. Mr. Dieckmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sulejic, are you able to confirm that, or is that part of the package which Mr. Yatvin still has to convey to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. SULEJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, unfortunately, I still don't know what the documents that are that I have that I received from Mr. Yatvin yesterday. It's all in English. This is not a problem for me, but I just need more time in order to acquaint myself with all the materials. So, at this point, I cannot be specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that will be clear in due course, once you have been able to go through the material. Thank you, Mr. Sulejic. When it then concerns the witness statements, i.e., Roman II of the same rule, we have touched upon that because that's part of only one pending motion that is before us. Rule 68, responsibilities exculpatory information is an ongoing obligation, and I take it that the Prosecution is well aware of that. I don't think we need to comment on it any further. There was a deadline set for inspection of books and documents and related materials under Rule 66(B), to be had not later than the 15th of October this year. I think this obviously for you, Mr. Sulejic. There is a need for you to take this as a priority, because that deadline obviously passed and you could not be held to it. So that was an example where we need to make a variation of the time-line for you, and I suggest the best way of doing it, instead of laying down a time, is that you relate and contact the Prosecution as early as possible and make arrangements for that requirement and that inspection to be had. Is that -- were you understanding, Mr. Sulejic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SULEJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour. This is a priority; and, of course, I'm going to use this instruction and this information properly. I have practically agreed with Mr. Harmon already that I would need to be in touch with the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. So we leave the matter at this point with that clarification. Thank you. And now we come to what I indicated before, the Rule 67, i.e., giving notice of any alibi. And just before I came into the courtroom, I had on my desk a filing as of yesterday, which entailed that the deadline laid down, which was yesterday, for giving such notice, was not, as far as Mr. Sredoje Lukic was concerned, possible to be met according to the filing. Mr. Dieckmann, would you like to address that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if I get an opportunity. As I explained yesterday, on the 65 ter conference, our team is trying very hard to go along with the order and the Rules to produce evidence we want to present. And in this notice, we are able to present alibi Defence regarding the counts 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12. Regarding the house burning on Pionirska Street, we have given alibi witness with addresses as it is set down in the Rule 67. But we have, up to now, practical problems to present it in the same proper way regarding the house burning in Bikavac; and, therefore, we respectfully request a short additional time, extension of time, for example, given a month, to produce it in the same accurate and proper way. The second point I would like to make, if you allow me, we are aware that we have to do it very fast and proper because we are in charge to defend a client who is in prison, and this was always the point of the Defence. To support the procedures, we are doing this as fast and as accurate as possible. But the representative of the Prosecutor, yesterday, told us that he cannot understand that it is not possible to present the alibi witness in due time, because the Defence knows the case since two years. This is the problem because from our point of view, of course, as defender you have information, or you are indications. But to produce evidence, this obligation for us starts in the moment when you receive disclosure from the OTP. Our case started from September 2007 and not two years ago; and, therefore, we respectfully request understanding and we definitely guarantee that we do everything possible to follow the next-to-last deadline we hopefully would get. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Dieckmann. Well, to me, Mr. Ossogo, there seems to be some merit to what Mr. Dieckmann is putting, but I'm happy to hear whatever comments you may have now, also being aware of the fact that you have time, obviously, in writing to respond to the motion. But, Mr. Ossogo, if you want to, I understand that Mr. Harmon, yesterday, was opposing, as Mr. Dieckmann also indicated, this particular motion. So whatever comment you have Mr. Ossogo, I'm happy to listen to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, as was under lined by my learned colleague, the Prosecution opposed this motion yesterday, for the reason set out by Mr. Dieckmann. After all, Mr. Sredoje Lukic received or had counsel for his Defence already two years ago. He was on notice of the indictment, which was made public when a co-accused, Mr. Vasiljevic, was notified of the indictment, so he followed the entire proceedings against Mr. Vasiljevic who was a co-accused. As a matter of fact, the accused, himself, has been put on notice for over two years of the charges against him. He was arrested in 2006, but he was aware of the charges beforehand, before that date. So he has been aware of all the facts for two years. There is a possibility of an alibi Defence, but the rule is very specific. That means that you claim not to have been there where the crime was alleged to be committed, and that cannot be invented over night. That's why Mr. Harmon said this yesterday. He said that it is not difficult to obtain witnesses to show that the accused was not there at a given place. So now there is a request for an extension of time; and out of courtesy, we're not against this principle of an extension, but we believe that a month is too much time. It is, of course, up to you, up to your wisdom, Judge, to decide to grant a shorter extension, so that we can start investigating once we receive information, because we will have to investigate to check the accuracy of the allegations made by the Defence as to the place where he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ossogo, for this very clear submission. I just want to make sure that you make this submission, not only on the back of what Mr. Dieckmann just said in Court, but you have also, I take it, studied and read the motion of yesterday. So your comments pertain to the written motion as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we did read the motion. We did not look at the CD-ROM we received. We are presently doing so, and it is -- part of the motion is applying for an extension. There is one incident, the Pionirska Street one; but now we're waiting for the other one, the one about Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ossogo. Well, in light of the fact that there may be issues linked to written motion which you just haven't studied, I will not rule on the motion at this point, but I would appreciate you write, then, your written answer to the motion; otherwise, I could have ruled on it. It seems that you still need time to study it. So we will decide on that in due course. That, of course, Mr. Dieckmann, given how things developed, you are actually given an extension, up until the point when we make a decision, and I urge you to make full use of that. Although, I also need to say to both parties, which I indicated there is obviously some merit to what Mr. Dieckmann is putting, because you could argue, as the Prosecution does as well, that this case has been worked upon, I suppose, for a number of years, but you also had a certain period on clarity and the clock didn't start to run when it came disclosure until a much later point. So I think, with that in mind, I'm obviously interested to read whatever the Prosecution is going to put then, in addition to what you said today. Thank you. With that, I think we could leave this matter. Were it not for the fact that for you, Mr. Sulejic, I think it is important to remember that you are in a slightly different position, and I would be happy, at this point, for the very fact that you're new to the case, and you are hereby ordered that not later than the 8th of January next year, submit the notice that you are required to do under Rule 67. Is that clear, Mr. Sulejic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SULEJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for your understanding. There's no need for me to explain anything, because you have put it yourself much better than I would have. I just wanted to stress that Mr. Harmon's position was that my client did have a -- an attorney who had received all the information and who could have conveyed that information to me. But I must stress, for the purpose of all other potential questions that may arise, it's clear to everyone, I hope - and if it's not, I need to emphasise this again - that my predecessor did not have the communication with my client that was required for reasons that I did not -- I do not want to go into now. So he didn't have any communication or contact with my client. So I'm going to do my utmost to meet all the deadlines placed by the Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sulejic. The Chamber takes comfort in your assurances. We have now reached a point, I think, where we only have to make sure, as indicated, that the times already laid down in the Work Plan, those times are noted by everyone, and I will just go through the times that are in the Work Plan. The first one is for the expert report according to Rule 94 bis to be filed, and the date for that is the 15th of February, 2008. The use of Rule 92 bis, ter, and quater summaries and motions on that are also to be filed on that date, i.e., the 15th of February. Adjudicated facts motion to be filed 29th of February, 2008. The Prosecution pre-trial brief should be filed not later than the 14th of March, 2008, and the Defence trial brief, i.e., for both of the Defences, to be filed not later than the 25th of April, 2008. With those dates, I think the case should then be ready for a pre-trial conference; and in the Work Plan, the date anticipated is the 16th of May, 2008. I take it by non-motion and silence that these dates square with the understanding of the -- of counsel on both sides. Nodding assent seems to be confirming this. Thank you. I have a question for the Prosecution -- oh, Mr. Ossogo, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. Just one specification as to the date of the 29th of February, I seem to understand in French. It was the 8th of February, with regard to the adjudicated facts. Are we talking about the 28th of February?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: It's a leap year, Mr. Ossogo. That's why the 29th, I believe. It's the very last day of February; and unless someone changed my calendar, I think it is the 29th, so the last day of February.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: The question I have, Mr. Ossogo, for the Prosecution is that it was indicated that the scope of the Prosecution case would be in the neighbourhood of six months, and I understand that this is -- these are early days, in a sense, because we have outstanding issues. I just want to make sure that whether there is an indication whether we could work on that assumption also today, the scope of the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely, Mr. President based on the Vasiljevic case. Because he was a co-accused, we had estimated six months. There was a slight extension of time, because precisely there was the Defence alibi that was raised. But, reasonably, the scope should be six months. It's a good work assumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that confirmation. The date when this case is actually going to go to trial is, as I have indicated at earlier Status Conferences, in the hands of the broader planning mechanism of the Tribunal. But I think it is fair to say, which I believe was also raised by the senior legal officer yesterday, to say that the earliest day for this case to be docketed is mid-2008, so in -- in the summer of next year, but it can also slide into later and even the early parts of the following year 2009. We have, as you know, other cases that are taking precedence, so this is what we can say at the moment, and I think counsel is aware of that. With that, and an eye to the times we have, I just want to indicate to the parties that I envision the next Status Conference in this case to be scheduled for sometime earlier March next year. That should be a date which could be conveniently fitted into the other time lines we have laid down in the Work Plan. Do counsel for either side wish to comment on this, or are you happy with this indication? This seems to be the case. Thank you. No need, Mr. Ossogo, if you're happy with it. If you're not happy, I am happy to listen to you, but you seem to be happy. Thank you. That, then, leaves me to ask whether the parties have any other matters to raise that we haven't touched upon, and I'm concerned of the obligation -- my obligation to ask the accused whether they have anything they wish to divulge or inform the Bench of, in relation to their situation, the conditions in the detention unit, and so forth. And if there are matters of a private narrate, we could move into private session if you want to take that up. So I turn to you first to you, Mr. Sredoje Lukic. Are there any matters that you wish to bring it my attention today? If you could stand up, please, and make the affirmation. THE ACCUSED SREDOJE LUKIC: [Interpretation] I have nothing specific to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Sredoje Lukic. Please sit down. Mr. Milan Lukic. THE ACCUSED MILAN LUKIC: [Interpretation] Everything is fine. I have nothing specific to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down. With that, any other matters from counsel? That doesn't seem to be the case by the shaking of heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSSOGO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, everything is fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much, Mr. Ossogo, for the courtesy. Thank you. Well, with that, I think we can call this Status Conference to a close, and we now stand adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
